conceptZh: 玩具機器人守門員擺出超認真的架式，飛撲出去撲了個空，足球慢悠悠地從他身下滾過去；他趴在地上抬頭看球，尷尬地比個讚。
object: a stubby toy robot goalkeeper with oversized foam gloves, and a chunky soccer ball
morph: the glyph 球 stands still as a solid sculpture while the goalkeeper gag plays out in front of its lower edge
creativeAngle: 孩子最愛的足球直接入題：笑點是「撲得超用力卻完全撲錯邊」的時間差，球慢到不行更好笑。球字筆畫多，所以讓字全程靜止當舞台，確保王部與求部結構不被動畫扭壞。語音詞「足球」的足ㄗㄨˊ已經學過，兩字都沒有破音問題。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid light cream background. One correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 球 stands centered the whole time as a flat-fronted sculpture in saturated deep grass green, filling about 70% of the frame height with comfortable margins on all sides. Use standard textbook proportions: the 王 radical on the left and the 求 component on the right stay clearly separated, with every stroke, dot and hook readable. The glyph never moves, rotates, tilts or gets covered, and the camera stays locked. In front of its lower edge crouches a stubby toy robot goalkeeper with oversized foam gloves, in an extremely serious ready stance, knees bent, visor narrowed. From 0.8 seconds a chunky black-and-white soccer ball rolls in slowly from the right, taking its time. At 1.6 seconds the goalkeeper launches into a spectacular full-stretch dive to the left, gloves outstretched, absolutely committed - and the ball simply trundles along under him to the right, completely unhurried. Hold on the robot lying flat on his face for a beat. At 3.2 seconds he props his chin up on one glove, looks sideways at the ball resting near the bottom-right corner, and gives a tiny sheepish thumbs-up with the other glove. By 4.6 seconds he has scrambled up, tucked the ball under one arm and bounced out of frame to the right. From 4.7 to 8.0 seconds the frame is completely still and clean, holding on the single centered 球 with nothing else in shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark or moody grading, no white blowouts. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「球、球、足球」, using the reading ㄑㄧㄡˊ for 球 both on its own and inside the word. Speak the first 球 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 足球 around 5.6 seconds while the finished glyph is held still, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep every sound effect soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not be added to the picture. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 球: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 自信滿滿的胖胖廚師熊把麵糰拋成圓球，卻接在自己的高帽上，帽子被壓成手風琴；最後輕輕一推，才成功抱住圓球。
object: An original rotund cartoon bear chef wearing a tall pleated chef hat, with one elastic ball of dough.
morph: The correctly formed glyph 球 remains a solid, stationary sculpture. One dough ball rebounds from the upper horizontal stroke of its 王 radical, squashes the chef's hat, and is finally caught.
creativeAngle: 用「麵糰變成彈跳圓球」連結字義，並讓王字旁的上橫成為反彈位置。廚師過度自信的大動作，換來高帽縮成手風琴的意外，最後用小動作成功接球，與前版守門員撲空明顯不同。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D animation in one continuous locked frontal shot. Against a light butter-yellow background, place one saturated cobalt-blue Traditional Chinese glyph 球 at the center, uncropped and approximately 70% of frame height with comfortable margins. Build it from a correct Taiwanese textbook glyph outline with shallow extrusion: preserve the distinct left 王 radical, the complete right 求 component, its upper-right dot, central hook, and all separate strokes and open spaces. Its front face remains crisp, stationary, and readable throughout.

An original rotund cartoon bear chef, with a tiny curled moustache and an extravagantly tall pleated chef hat, stands in the left margin beside the glyph. Keep the bear small enough to leave the letterform clear. The only separate prop is one smooth, elastic dough ball. Use rounded animated forms, soft studio lighting, and bright colors without neon or white glare.

At 0.0–1.0 seconds, the chef proudly rounds the dough between its paws, lifts its chin, and prepares an absurdly grand toss. At 1.0–2.2 seconds, it flings the dough upward with both paws, then closes its eyes and presents one paw for an effortless catch. Instead, the dough clips the exposed left end of the 王 radical's upper horizontal stroke and rebounds toward the chef. The sculpture stays perfectly rigid; the contact occurs at its outer edge without hiding the stroke layout. Pause briefly on the chef's smug waiting pose before the payoff.

At 2.2–3.3 seconds, the round dough lands squarely on the tall hat. The hat compresses vertically into a squat accordion while the dough remains perched on top. The chef opens its eyes, looks at its empty catching paw, then looks upward with a small surprised blink. Keep this soft and springy. At 3.3–4.6 seconds, the chef carefully nudges the dough from the hat into both paws, finally catching a neat round ball. It beams and takes quick little sideways steps out of the left edge, carrying the dough. The hat stays comically compressed.

From 4.6 through 8.0 seconds, hold completely still on the single centered 球, with the chef and dough fully off screen. Keep the background empty and every stroke sharply separated. The final clear hold lasts 3.4 seconds.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「球、球、圓球」. Pronounce 球 as ㄑㄧㄡˊ throughout. Say the first 球 around 0.4 seconds, the second around 1.4 seconds, and 圓球 around 5.5 seconds during the clear glyph hold, with natural pauses; stop after the word. Add only a quiet dough boing and a gentle hat squeeze, below the voice, with no music. The vocabulary is audio only. The sole on-screen writing is 球; use an unmarked costume and no subtitles, additional text, logos, watermarks, clutter, or flashing effects.
